[BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/n-able-takes-cloud-platform-offline-after-30-plus-zero-days-published/) reported that N-able took its cloud platform offline and urged on-premises customers to shut down servers following the public disclosure.

stories.title: France blames Iran for refrigeration sabotage attacks

reports.text: [Graham Cluley](https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/hotforsecurity/iranian-hackers-supermarket-freezers-france) reported that France officially accused Iran of responsibility for cyberattacks last month that meddled with supermarket freezers and caused some to catch fire.

[Infosecurity Magazine](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/france-blames-iran-supermarket/) reported that French authorities tied the cyberattack targeting supermarket fridges to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and requested international arrest warrants.

[The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/france-blames-iran-for-sabotage-attack.html) reported that an October cyberattack on refrigeration controllers at about 700 French retail sites was carried out by a cyber unit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

[SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/france-blames-iran-for-a-cyberattack-that-heated-supermarket-refrigerators/) reported that France summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions over the supermarket refrigerator cyberattack.

[The Register Security](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/09/france-blames-iran-for-supermarket-hack-meltdowns/5308591) reported that France blamed Iran for supermarket hack meltdowns describing it as the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory.

[The Record](https://therecord.media/france-blames-iran-for-fridge-cyberattacks) reported that French authorities identified the perpetrators as part of Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC cyber unit, and stated that some attacks caused fires.

[The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/us-agencies-warn-refrigeration.html) reported that U.S. government agencies warned that threat actors are actively targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems globally.

stories.title: Russian Turla group targets government Exchange servers

reports.text: [ESET WeLiveSecurity](https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/exchange-for-breakfast-turlas-cereal-tricks-are-not-for-kids/) reported on the Turla group's Cereal toolset, which features an Exchange email collection module, a command and control mechanism, and.NET execution techniques.

[Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/10/eset-turla-exchange-malware/) reported that the Russia-aligned group Turla planted a modular.NET toolset on Microsoft Exchange servers at two government organizations, one in Kazakhstan and one in Romania.
[Infosecurity Magazine](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/turla-cereal-exchange-email/) reported that Turla used compromised Exchange servers to collect NATO and EU-linked emails.

[The Record](https://therecord.media/russia-hackers-espionage-romania-kazakhstan) reported that Russian state-linked hackers compromised government email servers in Romania and Kazakhstan to secretly intercept messages exchanged with NATO and European officials.

[The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/russian-turla-hackers-use-new-cereal.html) reported that the Russia-aligned state-sponsored threat actor known as Turla is wielding a previously undocumented cyber espionage toolset called Cereal to steal emails from government Exchange servers.

[CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/russian-turla-group-used-new-toolset-to-silently-pilfer-emails-from-kazakhstan-romanian-governments/) reported that ESET published research on Turla's Cereal tools targeting Microsoft Exchange servers in the Kazakhstan and Romanian governments without obvious indicators of compromise.
